title: QuaLITi: Quantum Machine Learning Hardware Selection for Inferencing with Top-Tier Performance
problem: NISQ computers suffer from noise, long access queues, and high costs. QML algorithms are iterative and require multiple executions with defined shot counts, making single-hardware optimization impractical.
motivation: QML presents acceleration opportunity but hardware constraints (noise, queue depth, cost) limit practical deployment. Current practice relies on local simulators rather than real hardware due to access timing overhead.
method: The researchers train and test quantum machine learning models on several different quantum computers, each with different qubit types, connection patterns between qubits, and noise levels (errors in computation). They measure both how well the models work and how long users have to wait to access each machine, then analyze which hardware choice completes the training job fastest overall.
key_novelty: By switching between multiple quantum computers based on queue wait times, you can train quantum machine learning models with nearly the same accuracy but significantly faster than waiting for a single machine.
contributions: Multi-hardware QML training strategy reducing total wall-clock time
Empirical analysis of noise impact across different quantum hardware
Framework for optimal hardware selection based on queue depth and coupling maps
45X reduction in training wait time with only 3-4% accuracy impact
limitations: Abstract only; limited to small datasets (Iris, Digits); no details on specific hardware configurations or algorithmic modifications.
primary_theme: Quantum machine learning hardware selection and optimization
